title: Cross-site request forgery
summary: Cookies ride along on requests that other sites trigger. Stop forged requests with SameSite, tokens and origin checks.

steps.title: The confused browser
body: Cookies are attached by the **browser**, automatically, to every request for your site, no matter which page started it. That is what makes this attack work:
<!-- on https://evil.example, which Ada visits while logged in to your bank -->

The browser sends the POST **with Ada's session cookie**. Your server sees a valid session and moves the money. Mallory never saw the cookie; she didn't need to. This is **Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)**: the attacker borrows the victim's browser and its ambient credentials.
The attacker can *send* the request but cannot *read* the response (the same-origin policy blocks that). So CSRF is about **actions** (transfer, change email, delete), not stealing data.

steps.prompt: An API authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which the front-end JavaScript adds to each request. Why is it largely immune to classic CSRF?
options: Browsers never attach that header automatically, so a forged form post arrives without credentials
The same-origin policy blocks all cross-site POSTs
Bearer tokens expire faster than cookies
steps.explain: CSRF needs credentials the browser adds *by itself*: cookies, HTTP basic auth, client certificates. A token that your own script must read and attach can't be borrowed by another site. (It has other risks, covered in the JWT module.)

steps.title: Defences
body: Layer these; each covers gaps in the others.

1. **`SameSite=Lax` or `Strict` cookies.** The browser leaves the cookie off cross-site POSTs, which kills the form above. Lax still sends it on top-level `GET` navigation, so **never change state on `GET`**.

2. **Anti-CSRF token (synchronizer token).** At login, generate a second random secret and store it in the session. Your pages include it in forms (hidden field) or your script sends it in a header such as `X-CSRF-Token`. The server compares it with the session's copy on every state-changing request. Evil.example can't read your pages, so it can't learn the token.
3. **Check `Origin`** (or `Referer`) on state-changing requests: reject requests whose `Origin` isn't your own site.
4. **Custom header requirement** for JSON APIs: a plain HTML form can't add custom headers, and a cross-site script adding one triggers a CORS preflight that you won't approve.
ASP.NET Core has this built in: `builder.Services.AddAntiforgery()` and `app.UseAntiforgery()`, which Razor forms and Blazor use automatically.

steps.prompt: This function captures the browser's SameSite rules. What does it print?
code: bool SendsCookie(string sameSite, bool crossSite, string method, bool topLevel)
steps.explain: Lax blocks the forged POST but allows a cross-site link click. Strict blocks even that. Same-site requests always carry the cookie.

steps.prompt: Arrange the server's checks for a state-changing request protected by a synchronizer token.
lines: read the session id from the cookie
compare it with the session's token in constant time; mismatch -> 403
also: read the session id from the cookie
compare it with the session's token in constant time; mismatch -> 403
read the session id from the cookie
compare it with the session's token in constant time; mismatch -> 403
steps.explain: Authenticate first (401), then check the CSRF token (403), and only then act. When you read the header does not matter, as long as the comparison comes after the session lookup.

steps.prompt: Match each CSRF defence to why it works.
pairs: the browser leaves the cookie off cross-site POSTs
the attacker's page can't read the secret it must send
the browser reports which site started the request
plain HTML forms can't set headers

steps.prompt: Which change leaves an app **open** to CSRF even though its cookie is `SameSite=Lax`?
options: Rejecting POSTs whose `Origin` header is another site
steps.explain: Lax still sends cookies on top-level GET navigations, so a link or redirect to `/account/delete` from another site arrives authenticated. State changes belong on POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.

steps.title: Protect a transfer
prompt: The starter logs users in (ada / `correct horse`) and stores a `Session(User, CsrfToken)` with a random CSRF token for each session. `GET /csrf` returns `{"token": "..."}` to a logged-in user, the way a page would embed it. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.
Compare the token with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` on UTF-8 bytes.
starter: // Demo users. Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes, never as text.
var sessions = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, Session>();   // session id -> session
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, Path = "/",
ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string id && sessions.TryGetValue(id, out var s) ? s : null;
// TODO: 401 without a session, 403 without the right X-CSRF-Token header
return Results.Ok(new { sent = req.Amount, to = req.To });
// Unknown users still pay for one hash, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
solution: // Demo users. Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes, never as text.
var sessions = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, Session>();   // session id -> session
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, Path = "/",
ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"] is string id && sessions.TryGetValue(id, out var s) ? s : null;
if (!ok) return Results.Json(new { error = "Missing or invalid CSRF token." }, statusCode: 403);
return Results.Ok(new { sent = req.Amount, to = req.To });
// Unknown users still pay for one hash, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
hints: `var session = Current(ctx); if (session is null) return Results.Unauthorized();`
`ctx.Request.Headers["X-CSRF-Token"].ToString()` is `""` when the header is missing.
Return `Results.Json(new { error = "..." }, statusCode: 403)` on a mismatch.
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var c = NewClient(http);
await Dojo.TryAsync("The transfer could be checked", async () =>
var body = new { to = "bob", amount = 10 };
DojoWeb.Status("POST /transfer with no session gets 401", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", null, body));
var sid = await Login(c, "ada", "correct horse");
var token = DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/csrf", sid)), "token");
Dojo.Check("GET /csrf returns a token", !string.IsNullOrEmpty(token), "no token");
DojoWeb.Status("a forged POST (cookie, no token) gets 403", 403, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", sid, body));
DojoWeb.Status("a wrong token gets 403", 403, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", sid, body, "deadbeef"));
DojoWeb.Status("a token with one character changed gets 403", 403, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", sid, body, token![..^1] + (token[^1] == 'A' ? 'B' : 'A')));
var ok = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", sid, body, token);
DojoWeb.Status("cookie + right token gets 200", 200, ok);
var json = await DojoWeb.Json(ok);
Dojo.Eq("the reply says who was paid", "bob", DojoWeb.Prop(json, "to"));
Dojo.Eq("and how much", "10", DojoWeb.Prop(json, "sent"));
var sid2 = await Login(c, "grace", "hopper-1906");
DojoWeb.Status("ada's token doesn't work in grace's session", 403, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", sid2, body, token));
DojoWeb.Status("a token with no session gets 401", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/transfer", null, body, token));
static HttpClient NewClient(HttpClient http) =>
new(new HttpClientHandler { UseCookies = false, AllowAutoRedirect = false }) { BaseAddress = http.BaseAddress };
static string? SetCookie(HttpResponseMessage r, string name) =>
r.Headers.TryGetValues("Set-Cookie", out var values) ? values.FirstOrDefault(c => c.StartsWith(name + "=")) : null;
static string? ValueOf(string? header) =>
header is null ? null : header.Split(';')[0].Split('=', 2)[1];
static bool HasAttr(string? header, string attr) =>
header is not null && header.Split(';').Skip(1).Select(p => p.Trim())
.Any(p => p.Equals(attr, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || p.StartsWith(attr + "=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
static string? Attr(string? header, string attr) =>
header?.Split(';').Skip(1).Select(p => p.Trim())
.FirstOrDefault(p => p.StartsWith(attr + "=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))?.Split('=', 2)[1];
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient c, HttpMethod method, string url, string? sid, object? body = null, string? csrf = null)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(method, url);
if (sid is not null) msg.Headers.Add("Cookie", "sid=" + sid);
if (csrf is not null) msg.Headers.Add("X-CSRF-Token", csrf);
if (body is not null) msg.Content = JsonContent.Create(body);
return c.SendAsync(msg);
static async Task<string?> Login(HttpClient c, string user, string password, string? oldSid = null)
var r = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/login", oldSid, new { username = user, password });
return ValueOf(SetCookie(r, "sid"));
